summary.headline: Jyoti CNC Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 31% to INR588 crore with 28% EBITDA margin; order book at INR5,082 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue grew 31% YoY to INR588 crore, with EBITDA of INR164 crore (28% margin, up 320 bps) and PAT of INR115 crore (19.6% margin). Consolidated revenue rose 18.5% to INR602 crore, but consolidated EBITDA margin was 21.8% and PAT margin 12%, weighed down by Huron, where revenue recognition is pending end-user certificates and dual-use licences. Management said dispatches were about 1,900 machines, the highest quarterly volume in company history, and order intake was INR800 crore, taking the order book to INR5,082 crore. Management also disclosed PLI/ECMS approval for over INR1,020 crore of capex over five years with a 25% central capital subsidy (about INR255 crore).

segments.name: Standalone (machines)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR588 crore, EBITDA INR164 crore (28%), PAT INR115 crore. Entry-level machine sales INR1,802 crore (vs INR1,237 crore); 98 mid-range units (vs 69) and 11 high-end units (vs 9).

segments.name: Huron (Germany/France subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q2 dispatches about INR42-44 crore, but only about INR15 crore consolidated after intercompany elimination; about INR65 crore of prior revenue remains unrecognised pending clearances. FY27 Huron target about INR300 crore at 5-10% EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 Huron revenue target of close to INR300 crore (about EUR28 million), with H2 needing the bulk (about EUR6.5 million achieved so far).
Combined Jyoti plus Huron volume growth of 25-30%; machine volume target about 8,000 units for FY27 (3,317 achieved in H1, about 4,700 expected over the next two quarters).
Consolidated EBITDA margin target of about 25%, which management says it will reach by year end.
Huron dispatches expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27; Huron Q3 dispatches of INR80-100 crore were confirmed as a reasonable expectation.
FY27 capex outlay of INR450-500 crore; INR183 crore spent so far including advances.
Average realisation to be maintained at INR35-36 lakh over the next 2-3 years per management, though management earlier said INR32-35 lakh.
Operating cash flow to reach about 50% of EBITDA by year end.
Management expects 25-30% growth annually over the next 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Foundry (lost-foam vacuum casting, up to 15-tonne single castings) to commence in coming days; equipment in transit, completion expected this quarter. Foundry capacity to rise from 1,500 to 5,000 tonne per month.

ECMS/PLI electronics project: total cost INR1,250-1,300 crore over five years, with INR1,020 crore for machinery (25% central subsidy about INR255 crore; Gujarat state matching grant expected). First phase INR400-450 crore over one year, with about INR200 crore subsidy expected.
Controller division has over 110 engineers, with 40-50 more to be added over about six months; in-house CNC controllers, motors, drives and operator interfaces planned.
Huron new capacity added in November 2025; dispatches expected in Q3-Q4 FY27.
About 950 people added in the last six months.
demand_pricing: Order intake of INR800 crore in Q2; auto sector was over 50% of Q2 orders, with OEMs adding EV capacity. Q2 and Q3 are typically intake-heavy quarters.
Order book mix: aerospace and defence 36%, automotive 22%, general engineering 21%, EMS 12%, die and molds 4%.
Q2 revenue mix: aerospace and defence 21%, automotive 36%, general engineering 28%, EMS 7%, die and molds 1%, others 7%.
Management said imports still meet about 60-62% of Indian CNC demand; the company claims imports fell from about 80% a decade ago.
Management flagged global CNC controller supply tightness with delivery lead times more than doubled; company says it planned inventory buffers to manage this.
Management said the Japanese yen weakness has not lowered prices in India, as rupee depreciation offset the yen move.
EMS execution improved; Q2 output of about 1,900 machines against stated EMS capacity of 1,500 units.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still on track for Huron revenue of INR300 crore and what is the H2 dispatch phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR300 crore target and said about INR80-100 crore of Huron dispatches could come in Q3 with a ramp in Q4. Some end-user approvals have started, with 1-2 machine permits received recently.

qa_highlights.question: Will H1 interest cost fall to about INR14 crore despite higher net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the lower interest to working capital utilisation and said quarterly interest will remain stable, fluctuating with short-term borrowings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ECMS/PLI state subsidy expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the Gujarat state matching grant plus an R&D subsidy to take total subsidy above 50% of the INR1,020 crore outlay; sanction is expected soon.

qa_highlights.question: Are there French investigation or controller supply risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Huron investigation is at status quo with no communication since the April notice. Licence delays are a French-side issue, and controller supply is tight but has been managed through planned buffers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for machine realisation and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said average realisation is no longer the key metric, but gave a range of INR32-35 lakh; on margins, it said it will not go below 25% from the entry-level mix and expects H2 to be stronger.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cash flow and tax outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: OCF is about 47% of EBITDA, targeted at 50%. Management said the high Q2 tax rate reflects standalone economics and that consolidated tax should be viewed on a standalone basis; H2 employee cost to be similar to H1.

risks_watch: Huron revenue recognition: about INR65 crore of prior revenue and about INR250-300 crore of Huron revenue remain subject to end-user certificate and dual-use licence clearances, with the French investigation in status quo.
Execution: H2 needs about 4,700 machines and about EUR22 million of Huron revenue in two quarters; inventory days still about 190 (target below 200 and falling).
Supply chain: global CNC controller lead times have more than doubled as machine tool orders rise sharply in Japan, Germany, Italy and the US.
Margin mix: entry-level and auto machines dominate volume; management targets 25% EBITDA margin versus 28% standalone and 21.8% consolidated in Q2.
Aerospace and defence orders declined in Q2 due to delayed government tenders; management says the pipeline is intact.
Huron-based designs and the new controller business rely on execution of the in-house R&D team, and customer acceptance for in-house controllers is untested.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, capacity and margin targets, with the chairman answering most questions in detail. Evasive or vague on Huron revenue timing, the French investigation and specific cost/tax items, often redirecting to general statements.

growth.why: Management guides combined Jyoti plus Huron volume and revenue growth of 25-30% for FY27 with Huron close to INR300 crore, backed by a INR5,082 crore order book, record 1,911 machines in Q2 and foundry/ECMS capacity additions, though Huron revenue of about INR15 crore consolidated and INR65 crore unrecognised leave the Huron target dependent on H2 dispatches.
